_doc: Slice 5a (Task 1, the contract; eng OV9): the rules both lanes enforce, and every sentence `qbt search*` prints, so neither lane hand-copies a message. qbt (Task 2, tests/test_*.py) is the enforcing check and the window (Task 3, SearchView.js's node tests) only pre-checks; both must accept exactly the ok cases and refuse the rest with exactly the message given. See tests/fixtures/search-contract.md for the argv and JSON shapes. cases: {kind, input, ok, normalised?, host?, message?, why}; message is present only when not ok; why labels a failed assertion. Every rule reads the input exactly as given: nothing is trimmed first. BAD is the character class [\u0000-\u0020\u007f-\u00a0\u00ad\u1680\u2000-\u200f\u2028-\u202f\u205f-\u206f\u3000\u3002\ufeff\uff0e\uff61\\] (controls, every Unicode space, zero-widths, bidi controls, the soft hyphen, the IDNA dot variants U+3002, U+FF0E and U+FF61 (Ruling FG: in a host they would punycode into one label), and the backslash, which browsers read as /). Every URL kind is parsed by this text rule, never by a URL library (Ruling FB): the scheme (matched case-insensitively), then ://, then the authority, which is everything up to the first /, ? or # (or the end); then the path, from that / up to the first ? or #. An @ anywhere in the authority is userinfo. What's left is host[:port]: either an IPv6 literal, [ then hex digits, : and . with at least one : then ], optionally followed by :port; or a name with at most one :, the part after it being the port. A port is 1-5 digits with a value from 1 to 65535 (an empty port after : is refused). A name is lowercased, then each label with a non-ASCII character becomes xn-- plus its RFC 3492 punycode (no other IDNA mapping); the result must be 1-253 characters of labels separated by single dots, each label 1-63 of [a-z0-9-] not starting or ending with -, with no trailing dot. So a %-escape in the host, a trailing dot and an empty label are refused, and an IPv4 literal and a single-label host (localhost) are accepted as names. kind pluginUrl (qbt search-plugin install <url>; the window's i): checked in this order, the first failure's message wins: empty; more than 2048 code points; BAD or | anywhere (qBittorrent splits sources on |); not starting https:// (scheme case-insensitive); an @ in the authority (userinfo, OV12); a host or port the text rule refuses; the path's last segment (after the last /, before ? or #, not percent-decoded) not ending in .py (case-insensitive); the name (that segment without its last 3 characters) not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$. When ok, normalised is the plugin name qBittorrent gives the file (qBittorrent's naming: the last path segment with its extension dropped, query and fragment ignored; a % in it is refused so decoding never matters) and host is the host as the confirm shows it: lower case, IDN as punycode, no port. kind pageLink (d, design D3): empty; BAD anywhere (| is fine); not http:// or https:// (case-insensitive); userinfo; a host or port the text rule refuses. host as above. kind addLink (qbt search add <link> [<plugin>], OV5): input is the argv after `add`. A non-empty plugin must match the plugin-name rule (checked first); then the link must be free of BAD and non-empty. magnet:? (case-insensitive) -> normalised add (torrents/add; a plugin is ignored). https:// with no userinfo and a host and port the text rule accepts: with a plugin -> normalised plugin (search/downloadTorrent); without one (or an empty one), when the path's last segment ends in .torrent (case-insensitive, more than just .torrent) -> normalised add; anything else, http included, is refused. qbt also refuses a plugin that isn't in the current /search/plugins list (There's no plugin named <name>.), which a static case can't show. kind magnetHash (OV11, the library match): the magnet's xt / xt.N parameters, percent-decoded: urn:btih: with 40 hex, or 32 base32 (RFC 4648, either case) decoded to 40 hex -> v1; urn:btmh:1220 then 64 hex -> v2 (the sha2-256 multihash prefix stripped); prefixes are case-insensitive, hex is lowercased, the first of each kind wins. ok when either was found; normalised {v1, v2} with null for the missing one. An http(s) link never matches. kind row (OV9, OV12: sanitising lives only in SearchView.js; the sidecar passes rows through): input is one raw qBittorrent result; normalised is what the table shows before formatting: name is fileName with bidi controls (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) removed, C0/C1 controls (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F) each replaced by a space, then trimmed; over 300 code points it keeps the first 299 and adds …; empty or not a string is —. size (fileSize), seeds (nbSeeders), peers (nbLeechers): a finite number >= 0 as is, else — (qBittorrent's -1 for unknown, and anything that isn't a number: JSON has no NaN, so a string or null stands for it). published (pubDate, seconds): a number > 0, else — (qBittorrent sends 0 for none). kind pluginName (OV3; qbt search add, search-plugin uninstall/enable): ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$, never trimmed (qBittorrent trims names, so a space must be refused before it could); qbt also requires it in the current list. kind pattern (qbt search start --pattern): C0/C1 controls first, then empty after trimming. kind category (--category): exactly one of qBittorrent 5.2.3's category ids (searchpluginmanager.cpp categoryFullName). kind searchId (stop, delete): ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ and at most 2147483647 (qBittorrent's ids are rand(1, INT_MAX)). kind installReadback (A3, OV4): input {name, before, after} is the plugin's version in /search/plugins before the POST and at the end of the read-back (null when absent; the read-back re-reads every 0.5 s for up to 20 s and stops early once the name is there with a version different from before). sentences: every other line qbt search and qbt search-plugin print on stderr (exit 1), besides the messages in cases. <why> is qbt's API_FAIL (HTTP n, localhost auth is required, couldn't reach qBittorrent); <name> a plugin name; <version> its version. window: the window's own copy for Search (Task 3), in one place so the lanes and the final review agree.
